The problem

FOUR TAXES ON EVERY TOKEN YOU USE TODAY

Every prompt, every agent step, every product call — metered per token. Usage grows → bill grows. Linear. Success is penalised. ₹25L this month. More next month — growth works against you.
09:40 — repo read into the provider's KV cache. Paid in full: ₹430. 09:45 — five idle minutes. That's all the TTL allows. Cache evicted — the model forgets your entire codebase. Next question: full re-read, re-billed at 1.25–2×. Dozens of times a day.
Sprint week — 60 seats, agents running refactors, tests, migrations flat out. 5-hour window hits. Every seat throttled at once — mid-task. The cap doesn't know it's release week. Work stops; the clock doesn't.
Every request ships source code + customers' shipping documents off-site. Destination: shared multi-tenant GPUs you don't control. Your context sits beside other tenants' — retained on their terms. No audit trail, no deletion guarantee. The fourth tax is trust.

₹25L/month today — and the real cost isn't the bill. It's engineers waiting on cold re-reads, agents halted mid-sprint, and IP you can't account for.

The core idea

READ THE CODEBASE ONCE A DAY — NOT ONCE PER QUESTION

The 30-second version: an LLM re-reads everything from scratch for every question — and bills you for it. Its working memory is the KV cache. We build it once each morning and pin it in GPU RAM — the repo stays loaded, like RAM instead of re-opening every file.

09:45 — the whole codebase is read once into GPU memory (~5 min). Repo, schemas, customers' shipping docs — tokenised and pinned. Paid once. Never evicted. This is the whole trick.
10:00 — every question starts already-read. First token < 2 s. 60 developers + agents share one warm cache — no per-seat re-reads. 13:00 — coffee, standup, review. Nothing expires. TTL: none. Re-read bill for the whole day: ₹0.
18:00 — memory snapshotted to disk, GPUs released. You pay for working hours — not idle nights. 07:30 — restored in minutes, warm before standup.

Under the hood this is “prefix caching” (vLLM / SGLang) taken to its logical end: pinned, never evicted, single-tenant.

The model

GLM-5.2 — BUILT FOR EXACTLY THIS WORKLOAD

743B MoE · 40B active

Frontier-class capability, but only ~40B parameters compute per token — responses stay fast and cheap.

1M-token context

1,048,576 positions. Your 5M-token estate runs as 5–6 pinned shards (per service) behind a router.

44 KB/token cache

Compressed attention (MLA): the whole codebase ≈ 240 GB — pinnable in GPU RAM. Similar-scale models need several ×.

Sparse attention

2.9× lower attention cost at 1M context — answers stay snappy even against a huge pinned prefix.

MIT open weights

Official FP8 checkpoint. No lock-in to Z.ai — or to us. You can take the whole stack in-house any time.

Official 8×H200 recipes

First-party vLLM + SGLang serving configs on exactly the hardware we deploy. No exotic ops.

Released June 17, 2026. The open model the press calls “rivalling Anthropic” (Euronews, Jul 3). Don't take the press's word — the pilot is a two-week bake-off on your codebase.

Read the fine print

THE “BEST DEAL” SEAT IS SUBSIDISED, CAPPED — AND DRIFTING TO METERS

The seat is subsidised

Heavy agentic developers consume ₹40K–1.7L/month at API-equivalent rates on a ₹19K seat — real usage traces show 10–20× gaps. Vendors don't run negative-margin products forever.

The caps are the business model

5-hour rolling limits plus two weekly caps, shared across chat and Claude Code. Heavy sprints hit the wall mid-afternoon — squarely inside the IST workday.

The precedent is already set

GitHub Copilot launched flat “unlimited”, then moved to metered premium requests (June 2025). Anthropic added weekly caps (Aug 2025) citing round-the-clock agent use. The direction is metered.

Flat that stays flat

Our rate is structural, not promotional — we own the capacity on a locked hardware contract. Your usage can triple; the bill doesn't move.

15–20 devs, one 8×H200 node, real tickets, side-by-side with current tooling. GLM-5.2 runs with thinking enabled at reasoning_effort = max — you judge the model at its ceiling; we tune effort down for latency only after quality is proven. Architect tier (Fable) enabled for comparison.

Jointly review the metric gate. Pass → 2-week rollout to all 60 devs. Fail → we part friends; you keep the evaluation data.
